Studying accounting in Canada in 2027 can be a smart route into audit, taxation, financial reporting, corporate finance and broader business careers. The difficult part is not finding a Canadian university with an accounting course. It is choosing the right level, intake, cost, work experience and professional pathway for your situation.

If you are a school leaver, an accounting degree or Bachelor of Commerce with an accounting specialisation will usually be the natural starting point. If you already hold a degree, a Master of Accounting, Master of Professional Accounting or graduate accounting programme may be more efficient. College diplomas and advanced diplomas can suit students who want a more applied route.

There is a wide range of accounting courses in Canada for international students, from undergraduate degrees and graduate programmes to diplomas, certificates and selected online options. The Government of Canada’s EduCanada programme search lets prospective students explore Canadian colleges and universities by subject, study level, province and estimated tuition costs. Once you find a suitable option, check the institution’s own programme page for the latest entry requirements, fees, intake dates and delivery format before applying.

Why study accounting in Canada?

Accounting opens more doors than bookkeeping alone. Depending on your modules and later specialisation, you can move towards audit and assurance, taxation, financial reporting, management accounting, financial analysis or corporate finance.

A good accounting programme also builds wider business skills. Expect some combination of economics, statistics, finance, business law, information systems, spreadsheets and data analysis alongside core accounting subjects.

Work experience matters, too. Waterloo's Accounting and Financial Management degree, for example, is built around co-operative education rather than treating workplace experience as an optional extra. That is useful when you reach the graduate job market because you can point to real work rather than only a list of modules.

Accounting courses in Canada for international students

Bachelor of Accounting or BCom Accounting

For a student coming directly from school, a four-year undergraduate degree is usually the most straightforward route. You may see a Bachelor of Accounting, a Bachelor of Commerce with Accounting, a BBA in Accounting, or an accounting major within a wider commerce degree.

Common subjects include:

  • Financial accounting and reporting
  • Management accounting
  • Auditing and assurance
  • Taxation
  • Corporate finance
  • Economics and statistics
  • Business law
  • Accounting information systems
  • Data and business analytics

For applicants specifically looking for a bachelor of accounting in Canada, Carleton is a useful example because it offers a dedicated Bachelor of Accounting. Its published international undergraduate fees put the 2026-27 first-year cost at CAD 47,608.68, including compulsory miscellaneous fees. The university also publishes the same fee level, with a small difference for compulsory fees, across the following years in its current schedule.

Accounting diplomas and accounting colleges in Canada

College programmes are worth considering when you want practical skills, a shorter route or a bridge into further study. You will find Ontario College Diploma and Advanced Diploma options, post-degree diplomas and professional accounting certificates.

For example, George Brown Polytechnic's Business - Accounting diploma is a two-year programme with January and September starts, and its current international tuition listing shows CAD 19,261 for 2026-27. Its three-year advanced diploma follows the same broad accounting and business route and is also available for Winter 2027.

That makes accounting colleges in Canada particularly relevant for budget-conscious applicants. Still, never judge a course by tuition alone. Check the credential level, whether the programme is eligible for the outcome you want, and what happens after graduation.

Master's in accounting in Canada for international students

A master's is usually the more relevant search for a graduate who already has a degree and wants advanced or professional accounting study. Examples include Master of Accounting, Master of Professional Accounting, Master of Accountancy and Master of Accounting and Finance.

York's Schulich Master of Accounting is a good example of why current programme pages matter. The full-time MAcc starts in May 2027, and York's current programme information says the intake is being redesigned to align with CPA Competency Map 2.0. The current programme remains CPA accredited.

So when you compare masters in accounting in Canada, look beyond the course title. Check the academic prerequisites, professional alignment, length, tuition and the exact intake year.

Online accounting degree in Canada

Online study does exist, including undergraduate and postgraduate accounting options. Current programme directories list online accounting degrees and courses alongside campus-based programmes.

The phrase best accounting university in Canada sounds as though one institution must win. In practice, the better question is which programme gives you the right mix of curriculum, professional preparation, work experience and total cost.

University of Waterloo: a strong co-op choice

Waterloo's Accounting and Financial Management programme is particularly relevant to students who want structured work experience. Its co-op model means professional exposure is part of the degree design, not something you have to organise after graduation, as the university explains on its Accounting and Financial Management course page. That makes it a useful benchmark when you compare the best accounting programs in Canada.

McGill University: useful for the 2027 professional transition

McGill's Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting gives a clear example of why 2027 applicants need current information. For Summer 2027, McGill's admissions schedule says applications open on 1 November 2026, with an international deadline of 15 December 2026. The programme has limited enrolment, so meeting the minimum academic threshold does not guarantee admission.

York University: May 2027 master's route

York's Schulich MAcc starts in May 2027. York says the programme is being redesigned for that intake to align with CPA Competency Map 2.0, making it particularly relevant to graduates comparing professional master's routes.

Carleton University: a dedicated accounting degree

Students searching for bachelor of accounting Canada options should include Carleton in the comparison. Its international Bachelor of Accounting fee is currently published at CAD 47,608.68 for first year, with the university's 2026-27 fee schedule also covering later years.

Brock University: January 2027 postgraduate intake

Brock's Goodman School of Business is currently accepting applications for its Winter 2027 Master of Accountancy, with a deadline of 30 September 2026 according to the current MAcc admissions page. The programme is seven months full-time and is designed for the CPA pathway. A separate international professional accounting route begins in August 2027.

For a wider view of Canadian business-school ecosystems around accounting, it can also help to compare the business schools that dominate Canada's finance and management landscape before making a final shortlist.

2027 intake for accounting in Canada

September is a major intake for undergraduate study, but accounting also has January and May starts at selected institutions. There is no single national accounting deadline.

Current 2027 examples include McGill GCPA for Summer 2027, Brock MAcc for Winter 2027, York MAcc for May 2027, and George Brown Business - Accounting for Winter 2027. McGill's international GCPA deadline is 15 December 2026, while Brock's Winter 2027 MAcc deadline is 30 September 2026. The safest approach is to work backwards from the exact programme deadline and allow time for transcripts, English-language evidence, admission and study-permit steps.

Admission requirements to study accounting in Canada

Requirements vary by university, but applicants normally need a combination of:

  • A secondary-school qualification for undergraduate study or a relevant degree for postgraduate study
  • Academic transcripts
  • Mathematics or other subject prerequisites where the programme requires them
  • Proof of English-language ability where required
  • A statement, personal profile or supplementary application for selected courses
  • References for some postgraduate programmes
  • GMAT or GRE scores only where the specific programme asks for them

For accounting requirements for university, the important point is that there is no universal Canadian score. An IELTS 6.5 may be enough for one course and insufficient for another. The same applies to TOEFL and PTE.

Cost of studying accounting in Canada

There is no single accounting tuition fee for Canada. The spread is wide because a two-year college diploma, a four-year BCom and a one-year professional master's are different products.

The figures are useful for planning, not promises. Students on tighter budgets can also compare more affordable Canadian university choices before committing to a city or course. Universities can change fees, compulsory charges and fee schedules between academic years, so use the university or college fee page for your exact course when you are ready to apply.

That figure does not mean you will spend exactly CAD 23,448. Toronto and Vancouver can cost considerably more for rent, while a smaller city may let you manage accommodation differently. Build a realistic budget for housing, food, transport, books, insurance and an emergency reserve as well as tuition.

Cheap accounting courses in Canada for international students

Students often search for the cheap accounting courses in Canada for international students, but the cheapest tuition is not always the cheapest overall route.

College diplomas can be attractive because their tuition can sit below many university business degrees. George Brown currently lists CAD 19,261 in international tuition for its Business - Accounting diploma, while Durham College lists about CAD 15,489 for the first year of its accounting and business route. These are useful benchmarks, but the exact credential, city and post-study eligibility still matter.

Think about it this way: saving CAD 8,000 on tuition is not much of a saving if the course does not fit your long-term goal or carries different work-permit implications. Compare total cost, duration and outcome together.

Scholarships for accounting students in Canada

Always check the eligibility, closing date, whether the award is automatic or application-based, and whether it covers one year or the full programme. A scholarship that sounds large may be available only to a very small group of applicants.

CPA pathway after studying accounting in Canada

If becoming a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) is the goal, choose the degree and province together rather than treating the CPA stage as an afterthought.

Canada's professional accounting system is changing. CPA Ontario says the new CPA Professional Program will launch in January 2027, with a revised competency framework and updated requirements for new students; its current CPA guidance explains the transition. Its current guidance says applicants need a recognised degree or equivalent and at least 120 credit hours or equivalent to enter the new professional programme.

That change matters because many older web pages still describe the previous CPA PEP and CFE sequence as though it were the only 2027 route. It is not safe to copy those old steps into a 2027 application plan.

The right sequence is to check the academic prerequisites, identify the provincial CPA body you will use, confirm the professional education route for your intake year and then plan the required practical experience. Your accounting degree can position you well, but it does not by itself make you a CPA.

For students coming from abroad with an existing accounting qualification, the route can be different again. CPA Ontario's guidance for internationally trained accountants explains how previous professional education can affect the pathway. CPA Ontario maintains a separate pathway for internationally trained accountants, so previous professional membership and education may affect the assessment.

Working while studying accounting in Canada

Eligible international students can currently work up to 24 hours a week off campus during regular academic sessions, subject to the conditions attached to their study permit under IRCC's current work rules. During scheduled academic breaks, eligible students may work unlimited hours under the current rules.

For a student, the better use of work is not simply to cover bills. An accounting-related placement can build experience in accounts payable, audit support, bookkeeping, payroll, financial analysis or reporting. That experience can strengthen your CV when you start looking for graduate roles.

Still, do not make part-time work the foundation of your study-permit budget. Your financial plan should stand on its own.

PGWP after studying accounting in Canada

For graduates with a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree, the current federal guidance says there is no field-of-study requirement for PGWP eligibility, although other conditions apply, including the current language requirement set out in IRCC's PGWP eligibility guidance. Other university credentials can be subject to a field-of-study rule, so a shorter accounting diploma does not automatically produce the same result as a degree.

Accounting jobs and salary prospects in Canada

Accounting graduates can work in public practice, corporations, financial services, government and non-profit organisations.

Common roles include accountant, financial auditor, tax professional, management accountant, financial analyst, internal controls specialist, payroll specialist and financial reporting analyst.

Canada's Job Bank currently reports a CAD 40.36 per hour national median wage for financial auditors and accountants in its current wage report. That number is useful as a market benchmark, but it is not a guaranteed graduate starting salary. Pay changes with experience, role, location and employer.

The strongest candidates usually bring more than accounting theory. Excel, data interpretation, communication, business systems and practical judgement can make a real difference when employers compare recent graduates.

Study accounting in Canada for international students: what should you choose?

For a school leaver, compare a Bachelor of Accounting or BCom with accounting. For a graduate, compare MAcc, MPAcc and professional accounting programmes. For someone prioritising lower tuition and practical study, accounting colleges can make sense.

The key is to judge the course on more than rankings. Compare the curriculum, CPA relevance, co-op or work experience, 2027 intake, tuition, living cost, admission requirements and post-study eligibility in one place.

The counterintuitive part is that a lower-ranked university can be the better choice if its accounting programme gives you stronger practical experience and a more manageable overall cost. Ranking is a filter. It is not the decision.

FAQs about studying accounting in Canada

How many years does it take to study accounting in Canada?

A bachelor's degree normally takes about four years. College diplomas can take around two to three years, while professional master's and graduate accounting programmes can be considerably shorter.

What is the cost of accounting courses in Canada for international students?

Current published examples range from around CAD 15,489 for the first year of a Durham College accounting and business route to CAD 66,679 for the current UBC international BCom figure. Graduate courses often use term-based pricing, so compare the full programme cost.

What are the best universities in Canada for accounting?

Strong options include University of Toronto, UBC, Waterloo, McGill, York, Queen's, Carleton, Brock, Simon Fraser and University of Alberta. The best fit depends on study level, co-op, CPA pathway, budget and location.

Can international students study accounting in Canada?

Can I study accounting in Canada without IELTS?

Some institutions accept other approved English-language tests or grant exemptions. The exact rule belongs to the institution, so check the current programme requirement before applying.

Can I work while studying accounting in Canada?

Eligible international students can currently work up to 24 hours a week off campus during regular academic sessions, subject to the applicable conditions. Scheduled academic breaks can allow unlimited work for eligible students.

Can accounting graduates get a PGWP?

Some can. Bachelor's, master's and doctoral graduates currently do not face a field-of-study requirement, but they still need to meet the other applicable PGWP conditions. Other credentials can face additional field-of-study rules.

How do I become a CPA in Canada after studying accounting?

You need to meet the education, professional and practical-experience requirements of the relevant provincial CPA organisation. Because the professional education model is changing in 2027, check the pathway that applies to your intake year.

Conclusion

For students who want to study accounting in Canada in 2027, the strongest choice is not simply the university with the highest ranking. It is the programme that matches your academic background, budget, preferred intake, CPA plans and longer-term career goals.

Canada offers several routes into accounting, from undergraduate commerce and accounting degrees to graduate diplomas and master’s programmes. Start by comparing the exact course, current tuition, 2027 intake and professional pathway, then check the latest study permit and post-study work rules before you apply.

Final checklist for the 2027 intake

Before you apply, compare these eight things:

  1. Study level: Bachelor of Accounting, BCom, diploma, graduate diploma, MAcc or MPAcc.
  2. Programme fit: modules, accounting specialisation, analytics, audit, tax and finance content.
  3. Work experience: co-op, internship or structured placement.
  4. 2027 intake: September, January, May or another published start.
  5. CPA route: academic prerequisites and the provincial pathway that will apply to your intake.
  6. Career outcome: location, employer access and the skills you will leave with.

Once those eight points line up, the university ranking becomes much easier to interpret. Start with the programme you can qualify for and afford, then choose the institution that gives you the strongest route to your intended accounting career.
